_doc: Per-class WORK-SIGNAL spec. Each class states (a) what the fixture must contain for the
package's real code path to be reachable, and (b) the predicate that decides DID-WORK.
Predicate operators, evaluated against the delta produced by delta.mjs and the run log:
created_all_of  : every regex must match >=1 entry in CREATED (root:rel form)
created_any_of  : >=1 regex must match >=1 CREATED entry
changed_any_of  : as created_any_of but over CREATED + MODIFIED
min_created     : CREATED count over all roots must be >= n. WEAK BY CONSTRUCTION — it is
satisfied by 'the script wrote any file at all', including a bookkeeping
write from a script that then died. It must never be a class's ONLY
operator; see THE 2026-07-28 CORRECTION below.
created_binary  : >=1 CREATED entry is a REGULAR FILE of at least `min_bytes`. This asks
whether the script produced the substantial payload its class exists to
produce, not whether it produced anything. Executability and native-artifact
extension are RECORDED alongside each payload but do NOT gate the verdict —
see the class note. Implemented by isSubstantialPayload() in attribute.mjs.
content_nonce   : a CREATED/MODIFIED file matching `where` must CONTAIN the run nonce.
This is the ONLY operator a warm cache cannot satisfy, because the
nonce is generated per run and cannot pre-exist. Prefer it wherever
the class admits it.
log_match       : the combined stdout+stderr must match
STRENGTH is recorded per class and is not decoration: a verdict built on a weak signal
must be labelled weak in the corpus output, or the corpus overstates its own confidence.
── THE 2026-07-28 CORRECTION — read this before weakening any predicate ──────────────
The first full two-platform run reported 117 surviving verdicts on Linux and 96 on macOS.
115 and 94 of them respectively rested on a predicate satisfiable by 'the script created any
file at all': binary-downloader was created_any_of ['^(pkg|home|store):.*'] + min_created 1 —
a regex that reduces to `.*` after the harness strips its root prefix — and self-configuring
was min_created 1 alone. The class breakdown of the 117 was self-configuring 74,
binary-downloader 41, native-build-prebuilt 2, so the two STRONG predicates in this file (the
.o requirement for gyp builds, the content nonce for codegen) gated ZERO survivals. The whole
compatibility claim rested on the two weakest signals.
The proof that it was wrong rather than merely weak: @cloudflare/wrangler@1.21.0 scored
DID-WORK-AND-SUCCEEDED under the jail with changed=2, an IDENTICAL delta to its unconfined
arm, while its postinstall exited 1 on a denied host. And when those two entries were finally
printed rather than counted, they turned out to be worse than 'wrote a bit then failed':
.bin          0 b  dir      <- created by nub
.bin/rimraf 280 b  file     <- a PM-generated shim for wrangler's rimraf dependency
Wrangler's postinstall produced NOTHING. The predicate was reading the package manager's own
bin-shim bookkeeping as the package's work. Measured across one A0 shard, 135 of 140 owners
with any delta had .bin entries and 31% of all created entries were shims — so this was a
systematic inflator, not a wrangler quirk. delta.mjs now excludes node_modules/.bin from the
delta as PM noise, which is the deeper half of the fix; the predicate below is the other half.
So: binary-downloader now requires a binary-shaped artifact (created_binary), and
self-configuring is demoted to strength NONE / UNSIGNALLED. 74 honest 'we cannot tell' is
worth more than 74 survivals resting on min_created 1. Denial evidence is still harvested for
UNSIGNALLED classes — errsig.mjs scans every package's failures regardless of class — so
demoting a class costs the survival number but NOT the carve-out list, which is the study's
actual deliverable. Do not restore a work-signal for a heterogeneous class without a
per-package predicate written by hand and grounded in that package's own source.

fixture: No project files needed. The hazard is the opposite of a missing input: node-gyp
packages increasingly ship or fetch a PREBUILD and skip compilation entirely, which is
a bail-out of the path we mean to test. Force source compilation with
npm_config_build_from_source=true in the install env, and assert the .o evidence below.
why: The .o requirement is what separates COMPILED from DOWNLOADED. A prebuild-install
fallback produces build/Release/*.node with no object files at all, so an artifact-only
predicate would score a skipped compile as a successful one.

fixture: Cold download cache, and that cache directory MUST be inside a snapshot root (usually
$HOME or the package's own cache dir) or the download leaves no observable trace.
Set npm_config_build_from_source=false so the download path is the one under test.
why: No nonce is possible: the artifact is an upstream-fixed binary, so its content cannot
carry a per-run marker. The signal therefore rests entirely on CREATED-in-window plus a
verified-cold cache. State that dependency wherever the number is cited.

fixture: Cold per-package download cache, inside a snapshot root. Many of these consult a
*_SKIP_DOWNLOAD / *_BINARY_PATH env var; the env must be verified free of them, since
an inherited skip flag is a silent bail-out that scores as a pass.
why: A downloader's job is to land a USABLE BINARY, so the predicate names one. The prior
version said the corroborating signal 'is that the CREATED entry is a large executable'
and that the harness recorded size so it was 'checkable post hoc rather than baked into
the predicate' — the check was never performed, and 41 of 117 Linux survivals rested on
the unbaked version. It is baked in now.
Why the test is size on a regular file, and why the exec bit is NOT part of it:
* REGULAR FILE — a symlink is mode 0777 on Linux and dirs report size 0, so the type
must be pinned or every link the PM materialises would qualify.
* >= 1 MiB — the two distributions this separates are orders of magnitude apart and the
floor sits in the gap. Bookkeeping a bailing script writes (a JSON receipt, a log, a
saved HTTP error body) is tens of KiB at most; the real payloads are megabytes to
hundreds of megabytes (chromedriver, geckodriver, the Prisma engines, swc, dprint,
ffmpeg, pdfnet). The floor is not tuned to the observed pass rate — every package's
created-artifact list, with sizes and modes, is emitted into the report so the margin
is auditable and the choice refutable post hoc.
* NOT executability, and NOT a native-artifact extension. The first version of this
predicate required `>= 1 MiB AND (executable OR native ext)`, and that extra clause was
measured to produce a FALSE NEGATIVE on a genuine download:
azure-functions-core-tools@4.12.1 fetched a 579,911,350-byte payload at mode 0664 and
was scored INVALID-FIXTURE, i.e. 'unmeasurable', because 580 MB of successfully
downloaded binary happened to lack the exec bit. Calling a working downloader
unmeasurable errs in the direction that HIDES breakage, so both facts are now recorded
next to each payload and neither gates the verdict.
Why size alone is still sound: a >= 1 MiB regular file appearing in a cell that already
existed before the window cannot be materialisation (the `kind` discriminator separates
that), and cannot be the PM's hardlink-breaking either — rewriting a file with identical
content leaves digest and size equal, so it lands in TOUCHED, which is excluded from ACTED.
STILL NO NONCE, so the no-nonce caveat from the prebuilt class survives unchanged: the
artifact is an upstream-fixed binary and the signal rests on CREATED-in-window plus a cold
cache. What has changed is that it no longer ALSO rests on 'a file appeared'.
KNOWN LOSS OF SENSITIVITY, stated rather than hidden: a downloader that lands its payload
OUTSIDE its own store cell (into $HOME/.cache/<tool>/) is unattributable by path, so its A0
arm now fails the predicate and the row goes INADMISSIBLE instead of counted. That is the
safe direction — it reports 'cannot measure' rather than 'survives' — but it does hide a
real break behind an inadmissible row. Those writes are surfaced separately as
binary_writes_outside_cells in the report so the gap is visible.

fixture: The generator's INPUT must exist in the project — for Prisma a schema.prisma with a
generator block and a datasource block. Without it the postinstall exits 0 having done
nothing, which is the archetypal false pass this whole method exists to catch.
The schema MUST embed the run nonce (e.g. a model named NubProbe<RUNID>).
why: Content-derivation is unforgeable. A generated client carrying a model name that was
invented for this run cannot have come from a cache, a sibling arm, or a previous run.
This is the only class where the work-signal is immune to every cache trap by
construction rather than by hygiene.

fixture: A REAL .git directory — `git init` plus at least one commit, since some installers
check for a valid repository rather than the directory's mere existence. Also ensure
the fixture does not set core.hooksPath already, and that HUSKY / lefthook skip vars
are absent from the environment.
why: The effect lands in the project tree, which makes this class the sharpest probe of the
project-file grant axis: under a jail that grants no project access it must fail, and a
pass would mean the grant is wider than believed.

fixture: Nothing. The class has no input requirement, which is itself the problem.
why: HONEST GAP. This class produces no filesystem effect by design, so the tree delta is
empty on both the real and the bail path and cannot separate them. The only candidates
are an attempted-connect (needs a syscall trace, unavailable unprivileged on macOS) and
an exact stdout string (author-controlled, changes between versions, and absent when the
package detects a non-TTY or CI). This class is reported as UNSIGNALLED rather than
given a predicate that would manufacture false confidence.

fixture: Cold cache; and check for an 'already configured' short-circuit, which is the bail-out
shape for this class.
why: HONEST GAP, demoted from `weak` on 2026-07-28. The class is heterogeneous and has no
common artifact, and its predicate was `min_created: 1` — 'the script wrote any file at
all'. That supplied 74 of the 117 Linux survivals and 62 of the 96 macOS survivals, which
is to say the headline compatibility number was mostly this one line.
The prior text already contained its own refutation: it said the class 'must never be
counted in a succeeded figure without a per-package predicate written by hand'. No such
predicate was written, and it was counted anyway. Rather than invent one to keep the
number up, the class is now reported UNSIGNALLED — the same treatment telemetry-nag
already gets, and for the same reason.
This costs survival counts, not findings. errsig.mjs classifies failures for EVERY package
irrespective of class, so a self-configuring package that is denied a host or a path still
appears in the carve-out list with its denied host or path attached. What is gone is only
the unearned claim that it SUCCEEDED.
The route back to measurability is per-package, not per-class: name the specific artifact
each package configures (the file it writes, the config key it sets) from that package's
own published source, and give it its own predicate. That is real work and it is the only
honest way to recover these rows.
